title: The Vanishing WIMP Parameter Space
bottleneck: The WIMP 'miracle' motivated dark matter models for decades, but direct searches, LHC missing-energy analyses, and Fermi-LAT dwarf-galaxy gamma-ray limits have excluded most of the canonical thermal-relic cross-section range. Theorists keep retreating to tuned corners (resonances, co-annihilation, very heavy or very light WIMPs), yet no positive signal has appeared anywhere. Collider searches face the same wall: the LHC has excluded large swaths of simplified WIMP models, and even a future 100 TeV collider would leave light-mediator scenarios untouched.
why_it_blocks: Each retreat narrows the flagship dark matter paradigm without replacing it, leaving model-building drifting and experimental programs chasing ever-smaller windows.
current_state: Fermi-LAT and HESS constrain annihilation; LZ/XENONnT constrain scattering; the remaining thermal WIMP window sits at TeV masses probed only by future colliders and CTA. Attention is drifting toward non-thermal histories and hidden sectors, but the field lacks a unifying candidate to replace the WIMP's former centrality.
